data.title: Uranium Energy started Sector Perform, Speculative Risk at RBC amid risks to ambitious plans
data.description:
Uranium Energy (UEC) down 0.6% in Friday's trading as RBC Capital initiated coverage with a Sector Perform rating with a Speculative Risk qualifier and a $10 price target, seeing the shares as fairly valued, reflecting strong growth potential but balanced against execution risk.

Uranium Energy (UEC) holds the largest licensed U.S. uranium capacity at 12M lbs/year, with production currently ramping, which could generate significant cash flow at RBC's ~$110/lb long-term uranium price forecast, but analyst Andrew Wong said he sees ramp-up risks related to labor, permitting, and construction.

Wong noted Uranium Energy (UEC) is ramping up uranium production in Wyoming and Texas, developing the Roughrider project in Saskatchewan, and plans to build new uranium conversion capacity in the U.S., and he thinks the company offers highly leveraged exposure to uranium, especially U.S.-origin, but also potential execution risks given its ambitious and expansive plans.

"We see the industrial logic, U.S.-origin benefit, and need for more domestic conversion capacity," Wong wrote, but added that "building greenfield conversion in the U.S. comes with significant risks, and plan details are currently limited."

data.title: DOJ won't reopen criminal probe into former Fed chair Powell - report
data.description:
The Department of Justice isn't reopening a criminal investigation into former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell for cost overruns at the central bank's building renovations project, U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said in an interview on Friday.

In an interview with Bloomberg News, Blanche said he's satisfied with the  Fed's Inspector General report that found no evidence of criminal wrongdoing by Powell regarding the renovation. 

But the head of the Justice Department didn't rule out continuing to examine the project's oversight and potentially take action if evidence of wrongdoing emerges, the article said.

"We're not reopening a criminal investigation into him," Blanche said in the interview.

The Fed said it will hire an independent auditor to study the building costs. If that review finds evidence of criminal actions, then the Justice Department could investigate, he said.

Powell took the unusual action of remaining on the Federal Reserve Board even after his term as chairman ended. Fed chairs traditionally resign after their terms end. Powell's term as chair ended in May 2026, but his term as a governor ends on Jan. 31, 2028.

In April,  Powell said he'll stay on the board until the DOJ investigation is "well and truly over." That decision has frustrated President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly said Powell should quit and accused him of acting politically.

Blanche's comments that the DOJ may take up the investigation may not instill the confidence that Powell would need to walk away with the knowledge that the Fed's independence is ensured.

data.title: OpenAI hires former Trump cybersecurity adviser: report
data.description:
• OpenAI (OPENAI) has hired Thomas Lind, a former cybersecurity adviser to the Trump Administration, The Information reported.
  • In his role at the ChatGPT maker, Lind will lead a team focused on cyber and strategic risk as part of its national security policy team, the news outlet added. Lind joined the company this week, the news outlet explained.
  • OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Seeking Alpha.
  • Before joining OpenAI, Lind held several roles in the Trump administration, including most recently as head of policy and senior advisor to the Director. In this role, which he held for three months, he was the senior White House official responsible for AI and cybersecurity policy. He helped develop the administration’s AI security framework and cybercrime strategy, including a major executive order on AI, an executive order on cybercrime, and more. 
  • Lind also spent more than three years at the National Security Agency working on a number of different initiaitves.

data.title: Boeing MAX 10 moves closer to certification after FAA software review
data.description:
U.S. aviation regulators have found that a software problem affecting some Boeing (BA) 737 MAX flight computers does not create a flight-safety concern, removing a regulatory obstacle to certification of the MAX 10.

A panel of safety experts at the Federal Aviation Administration concluded that the issue did not pose a safety risk because pilots continue to have full control of the aircraft and receive clear and unambiguous indications, the agency said on Friday.

The software problem can arise when a pilot abandons a landing and requires the autopilot to shift to a less automated mode for pitch control, increasing the workload for the flight crew. The FAA had paused certification of the MAX 10 earlier this week while it reviewed the issue. The agency approved the smaller MAX 7 in August despite the affected software being present.

The MAX 10, Boeing's (BA) largest 737 MAX variant, is already years behind schedule and has more than 1,500 orders. The FAA said it would assess whether any further action was necessary.

Boeing (BA) shares were trading about 2.5% higher on Friday.

data.title: OKLO, BKH draw highest short interest in utilities sector; RNW and SRE see lowest short interest
data.description:
Within the utilities sector (XLU), short sellers remain heavily concentrated in electric utilities, with several electricity producers and multi-utility companies ranking among the most heavily shorted stocks in the market at the end of September.

The utilities sector (XLU) comprises companies involved in providing services such as electricity, natural gas, and water, among others.

Oklo (OKLO) recorded the highest short interest among utilities stocks with a market capitalization of more than $2B, with short interest representing 18.09% of shares outstanding. The company’s shares have slipped more than 48% year to date, underperforming the benchmark S&P 500, which has gained more than 12% over the same period.

Oklo was followed by Black Hills (BKH) at 14.20%, reflecting elevated bearish positioning in both stocks.

At the other end of the spectrum, ReNew Energy Global (RNW) and Sempra (SRE) were among the least shorted utilities stocks, with short interest of 1.09% and 1.68%, respectively.

data.title: Apple updates Full Disk Access controls in macOS in response to probing AI agents
data.description:
Apple (AAPL) plans to update its controls regarding "Full Disk Access" in macOS in response to artificial intelligence agents potentially probing all available avenues of user data.

The Cupertino-based company warned that developers using "Full Disk Access" can expose everything on their systems to personal AI agents, including files, mail, private messages and browsing history. This not only creates potential privacy issues for the user but also for those a user communicates with.

"Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action," Apple said in a developer update on Friday. "Addressing this is critical. As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially. We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy."

The update follows potential concerns over Meta's (META) Muse app. Last month, tech columnist Jason Aten wrote a piece for Inc. that his Muse AI agent was reviewing his private messages and emails even though he had not given it permission to do so.

In one example, he said Muse sent him a push notification suggesting that a text message conversation he was having with his co-host would make for a good column. It even offered to start researching the topic. It also flagged another private message he had exchanged with his editor days prior about the proposed column's due date.

"Not only had I not asked it to do that sort of thing, I never gave it permission to read my messages," Aten wrote. "In fact, I remember explicitly choosing not to let it have access to my messages, calendar, and other personal information."

data.title: BNY in talks with Kraken parent for digital asset infrastructure pact - report
data.description:
BNY (BNY), the custody bank powerhouse, has entered talks with Payward, the parent of crypto exchange Kraken (KRAKEN), to form a broad partnership encompassing digital assets and financial market infrastructure, according to a media report on Friday.

The potential partnership may offer crypto products, custody, wealth management, trading, payments, and infrastructure, CoinDesk reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. Talks are ongoing, and there's no guarantee that a deal will be reached.

Parts of the proposed agreement could be similar to the infrastructure component of Payward's recent partnership with Nasdaq, one of the people told CoinDesk.

An agreement would advance Payward's progress to connect its digital-asset operations with established financial institutions. From a broader perspective, it would underscore the inroads that digital assets are continuing to make into more traditional financial systems.

BNY (BNY) stock rose 1.3% in Friday afternoon trading.

Last month, Nasdaq (NDAQ) agreed to invest $100M  in Payward as they expand their partnership to develop infrastructure for tokenized markets. Kraken is set to distribute Nasdaq's tokenized stocks on its platform, giving investors access to Nasdaq-listed stocks in tokenized form.
